bottleneck.description: #2 spine surgical robotics platform (ExcelsiusGPS) in a clearly contested 4-5 player market against Medtronic Mazor, J&J VELYS, Stryker Mako Spine, and Zimmer Rosa Spine.

dependency.key_customers: Hospitals, ambulatory surgery centers (orthopedic surgery departments), spine surgeons
dependency.key_suppliers: Component suppliers for navigation cameras, robotic arms, contract manufacturers; pull-through with Globus implants/spinal hardware

editorial.notes: Spine robotics is a peer-competitive oligopoly: Medtronic leads at ~22-24% share, Globus at ~16-18%, with J&J/Stryker/Zimmer all selling viable alternatives. While individual hospitals face real capital switching friction ($700K-$1.5M systems plus surgeon retraining), the market has 4-5 credible substitutes and no single platform is structurally indispensable. Globus's value comes from scale, IP, and integrated implant pull-through, not from being a sole-source bottleneck. Matches LOW calibration of peer-competitive system integrators (ABBN, 6954, ROK, SYM).
